title: High-resolution ALMA observations of compact discs in the wide-binary system Sz 65 and Sz 66
question: Whether compact protoplanetary discs around the wide-binary stars Sz 65 and Sz 66 exhibit substructures on spatial scales of ~4 au

data.sensitivity: 13 μJy/beam (continuum); 1.9 mJy/beam km/s or 1.81 mJy/beam.km/s (12CO cube, 1 km/s channels); 10 mJy/beam.km/s (unthresholded moment 0)

what.value: Stellar masses of 0.76 ± 0.18 M_sun for Sz 65 and 0.31 ± 0.04 M_sun for Sz 66 from X-shooter spectroscopy

evidence.quote: Based on an analysis of X-shooter spectroscopy, stellar masses of 0.76 ± 0.18 M⊙ were calculated for Sz 65 and 0.31 ± 0.04 M⊙ for Sz 66 (Alcalá et al. 2014, 2017).

what.value: Gaia distances of 153.0 ± 0.6 pc for Sz 65 and 154.4 ± 0.6 pc for Sz 66

evidence.quote: Their Gaia distances are very similar, 153.0 ± 0.6 pc for Sz 65 and 154.4 ± 0.6 pc for Sz 66 (Bailer-Jones et al. 2021)

what.value: ALMA Band 7 (890 μm) continuum fluxes of 64.49 ± 0.32 mJy (Sz 65) and 14.78 ± 0.29 mJy (Sz 66) used for spectral index calculation

evidence.quote: The discs were previously observed as part of the Lupus survey with ALMA at 890 μm (angular resolution ~ 0''.30), where continuum fluxes of 64.49 ± 0.32 and 14.78 ± 0.29 mJy were measured (Ansdell et al. 2016)
For Sz 65, the flux measured in Band 7 (890 μm) by Ansdell et al. (2016) was 64.5 mJy, which gives a spectral index α = 2.3 ± 0.3

what.value: Radial brightness temperature profiles of DSHARP survey discs and CX Tau for comparison

evidence.quote: The top panel in Figure 13 compares the TB (R) profile for Sz 65 and Sz 66 with the DSHARP sample and CX Tau (Facchini et al. 2019).

external_data.citation: Andrews et al. (2018a,b), Facchini et al. (2017, 2019)

recipe.goal: Align, self-calibrate, concatenate, and image continuum and 12CO datasets
recipe.method: Individual phase/amplitude self-calibration in CASA, Gaussian fit to align phase centres to J2000 15h39m27.750s -34d46m17.692s, concatenation of 4 continuum datasets and 2 CO datasets, and Hogbom CLEAN with Briggs robust=0.0 (plus 0''.07 uv taper and Keplerian masking for CO)
key_parameters: robust = 0.0 (also tested -2.0 and 2), uv taper = 0''.07 for CO, channel width = 768 kHz (1 km/s) for CO, solint = 30s (2019.1.01135), solint = 120s (2017.1.00569), applymode = 'calonly' (2018.1.00271, 2018.1.01458)

recipe.goal: Measure image-plane continuum and CO fluxes, disc geometry, radial profiles, R90 sizes, spectral indices, and dust masses
recipe.method: 2D Gaussian fitting in the image plane for PA and inclination, deprojecting and azimuthally averaging surface brightness for 1D profiles and cumulative 90% flux radii (R90), integrating moment 0 maps above 3σ, combining with Band 7 fluxes for spectral index, and computing optically thin dust mass
key_parameters: 3σ contour threshold for integrated continuum flux and moment map creation
assumptions: Optically thin thermal dust emission, distance d = 153 pc (Sz 65) and 154.4 pc (Sz 66), midplane temperature T = 20 K, dust opacity κ_ν = 0.1 (ν/10^12 Hz)^β cm^2 g^-1 with β = 1.0, 10% flux calibration uncertainty

recipe.goal: Non-parametric visibility modelling of 1D radial continuum brightness profiles
recipe.method: Fit deprojected real visibilities in logarithmic brightness space using frank (log-normal method), testing hyperparameter variations and phase centre offsets
key_parameters: Maximum radius R_max = 2'', number of collocation points N = 300, hyperparameter α = 1.2 (also tested α = 1.05, 1.30), wsmooth varied, phase centre shift grid up to ±5 mas (best shift dRA +1 mas, dDec -4 mas)
assumptions: Axisymmetric 1D disc brightness distribution; power spectrum prior applied to log(I_ν)

recipe.goal: Kinematic modelling of 12CO (2-1) rotation velocity maps
recipe.method: Create peak velocity maps from the 1.0 km/s cube above 3σ using bettermoments, and fit Keplerian rotation models (with an elevated flared emission surface for Sz 65, flat for Sz 66) using eddy MCMC
key_parameters: robust = 0.0 cube, 1.0 km/s spectral resolution, 3σ threshold; for Sz 65 final fit: fixed inclination = 63.76◦, M_* = 0.76 M_sun, d = 153.1 pc; for Sz 66 fit: fixed M_* = 0.31 M_sun, d = 156.0 pc
assumptions: Keplerian rotation; for Sz 65 an azimuthally symmetric elevated emission surface z(r) = z0 * (r/1'')^ψ * exp(-(r/r_taper)^q_taper)

recipe.goal: Probabilistic modelling of binary tidal truncation radii
recipe.method: Compute probability distributions P(R_t) of equilibrium tidal truncation radii using the Pichardo et al. (2005) semi-analytical formula and Torres (1999) deprojection via Monte Carlo sampling of orbital parameters
key_parameters: 10^6 Monte Carlo realizations per case; uniform eccentricity priors [0.0, 0.7] and [0.0, 0.9]; mass ratio q = M_Sz65 / M_Sz66 (and inverted for Sz 66)
assumptions: Disc midplane lies on the binary orbital plane; uniform eccentricity distribution; sin(i) orbital inclination distribution

recipe.goal: Estimate upper limit on gap-opening planet mass in Sz 65 and compare brightness temperature profiles with DSHARP
recipe.method: Apply the Lodato et al. (2019) Hill-radius gap-width scaling relation to the frank gap/ring locations in Sz 65, and compute radial brightness temperature T_B(R) profiles to compare against DSHARP and CX Tau
key_parameters: Gap minimum at r = 20 au, ring peak at 24 au, gap width ∆ = 4 au, scaling constant k = 4.5 - 8, stellar mass M_* = 0.76 M_sun
assumptions: Low disc viscosity (α < 0.01); gap width scales with planet Hill radius

score_reason: All five ALMA project codes, the common phase centre coordinates, weighting/taper parameters, and analysis packages (CASA, frank, eddy, bettermoments) are clearly specified, along with key frank and eddy parameters; minor deductions for missing self-cal solints on the long-baseline EBs, CLEAN pixel/masking parameters, and internal text typos on Sz 66 flux.
rediscovery_reason: All five ALMA datasets are public in the archive, the data reduction and visibility/kinematic modelling recipes use standard open-source tools (CASA, frank, eddy, bettermoments), and the main findings (Sz 65 gap at 20 au, ring at 24 au, R90 sizes, and kinematic stellar mass) are quantitative.
